salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-senhor.context: Psalm 13 is a prayer of lament. The psalmist repeats questions to God amid sorrow and the enemy, asks God to look at him and ends trusting in grace.
salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-senhor.focusQuestion: What do you need to say honestly to God today, instead of keeping it in silence?
salmos-lamento-01-ate-quando-senhor.keywordGloss: The repeated question of one who suffers and brings the delay to God in prayer, without hiding the pain.
facts: The psalmist asks how long the Lord will hide his face from him.
He feels sorrow in his heart day after day.
He asks the Lord to light up his eyes.
He asks that the enemy not claim victory over him.
He trusts in the Lord's grace.

salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mim-um-cora.context: Psalm 51 is a prayer of repentance. The psalmist asks for cleansing from sin, a pure heart created by God, the Spirit's presence and the joy of salvation back.
salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mim-um-cora.focusQuestion: What do you need to ask God to create anew in you, instead of just promising to try harder?
salmos-lamento-02-criai-em-mim-um-cora.keywordGloss: The central request of the Psalm: that God do within what the psalmist cannot do alone.
facts: The psalmist asks for purification and says he will be clean.
He asks God to blot out all his iniquities.
He asks for a pure heart created by God.
He asks not to be cast away from God's presence.
He asks for the joy of salvation back.
Once renewed, he will teach God's ways.

salmos-lamento-03-desafio-orar-os-salm.context: This challenge brings together two prayers from the Psalms: the lament that asks how long and the repentance that asks for a pure heart. Here, praying is bringing pain and guilt to God.
salmos-lamento-03-desafio-orar-os-salm.focusQuestion: Which of these two prayers do you most need to make your own today: lament or repentance?
salmos-lamento-03-desafio-orar-os-salm.keywordGloss: Speaking to God with honest lament, repentance and trust in his grace.
facts: The psalmist asks how long the Lord will hide his face from him.
After the lament, he trusts in the Lord's grace.
The repentant one asks for purification and says he will be clean.
He asks for a pure heart created by God.
He asks for the joy of salvation back.
Renewed, he will teach God's ways to others.

salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventurado-o-hom.context: Psalm 1 opens the book of Psalms by presenting two paths for life. It contrasts the company and counsel the man avoids with the delight he finds in the law of the Lord.
salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventurado-o-hom.focusQuestion: Which voices have been guiding your choices, and how much room does God's word have in your day?
salmos-louvor-01-bem-aventurado-o-hom.keywordGloss: This is what the text calls one who lives on God's path, delighting in his law.
facts: The blessed one does not walk in the counsel of the wicked.
The blessed one does not sit in the circle of mockers.
The blessed one's delight is in the law of the Lord.
He meditates on the law of the Lord day and night.
The Lord is presented as the shepherd of those who trust in him.

salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o-meu-pas.context: Psalm 23 is a prayer of trust that uses the image of the shepherd and the sheep. The psalmist speaks of provision, rest, presence in danger and goodness that follows him.
salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o-meu-pas.focusQuestion: In what area of your life do you need to trust the Lord's care as shepherd today?
salmos-louvor-02-o-senhor-e-o-meu-pas.keywordGloss: An image of God who provides, guides, protects and is present with his people.
facts: With the Lord as shepherd, the psalmist says he will lack nothing.
The Lord makes him lie down in green pastures.
The Lord guides him in paths of righteousness.
In the valley, the Lord is with the psalmist.
The Lord prepares a banquet for him before his enemies.
Goodness and mercy will follow him all his days.
